conventions.convention: Reconstruction uses the normalized finite continued fraction, includes its terminal convergent, requires N ≥ 1 and Q > 4N², and accepts exactly when 1 ≤ q ≤ N and 2|yq − pQ| ≤ q.
The finite-rational Legendre bridge requires reduced fractions, positive denominators, D > 2q, and the strict inequality |A/D − p/q| < 1/(2q²).
Nearest phase labels are defined using circular distance; reconstruction correctness separately removes endpoint wrapping for nonzero reduced k/r and treats k = 0, r = 1 explicitly.

The modular multiplier fixes invalid n-bit encodings and control-zero inputs. Registers use most-significant-first port order, while internal arithmetic arrays are indexed from least significant bit zero. Work registers are clean.
Order finding takes N ≥ 3, a standard unit representative, and integer b ≥ 1; it sets n = ceil(log₂N), m = 2n + 3, Q = 2^m, and t = 4(n + 1)b.
Each order-finding sample starts from |1⟩, uses the QPE gate list through its superposition law, retains a denominator only after x^q = 1 modulo N, and returns the smallest retained denominator.

Gate bounds use ideal exact arbitrary-angle QFT gates. Compiled modular-multiplier calls, bare controlled-U queries, gates, and multitape classical transitions are separate coordinates; no finite-alphabet, uniform-family, or generator-time bound is asserted.

load_bearing.statement: For integers N ≥ 1, m ≥ 0, Q = 2^m > 4N², 1 ≤ r ≤ N, and 0 ≤ k < r with gcd(k,r) = 1, every nearest circular grid label y reconstructs k/r. For every phase label y, there is at most one passing candidate with denominator at most N.

For N ≥ 3 and a unit x modulo N of order r, one independent phase sample yields denominator r with probability at least (4/π²)φ(r)/r ≥ 4/[π²(1 + log₂N)]. With b ≥ 1, after t = 4(n + 1)b independent samples the algorithm returns the exact order with probability at least 1 − 2^(−b). For any 0 < δ < 1, b = ceil(log₂(1/δ)) gives success probability at least 1 − δ.

For N ≥ 2, n = ceil(log₂N), and a unit a modulo N with supplied inverse, the specified circuit is unitary, fixes the control, multiplies valid z by a when c = 1, fixes z otherwise, restores all Boolean value, target, and scratch registers to zero, and extends coherently to superpositions.
Let A,p be integers and D,q positive integers, with A/D and p/q reduced and D > 2q. If |A/D − p/q| < 1/(2q²), then p/q is a convergent of the normalized finite regular continued fraction of A/D.
Let N ≥ 1, Q > 4N² be integers and 0 ≤ y < Q. There is at most one reduced fraction p/q with 1 ≤ q ≤ N satisfying 2|yq − pQ| ≤ q.

For N ≥ 2, n = ceil(log₂N), and a standard representative of a known unit, each explicit controlled constant multiplier has S,E = O(n²), uses O(n²) elementary gates and clean work bits after reversible compilation, and O(n) repeated-squaring constants and inverses can be computed in O(n³) deterministic multitape bit transitions. No depth bound is asserted.
For every integer r ≥ 1, φ(r)/r ≥ 1/(1 + log₂r), with φ(1) = 1.

For integers N ≥ 1, m ≥ 0, Q = 2^m > 4N², and 0 ≤ y < Q, set L = ceil(log₂(Q + 1)). The reconstruction algorithm uses O(L) Euclidean divisions and O(L³) deterministic multitape bit transitions, without real-number arithmetic.

For N ≥ 3, n = ceil(log₂N), b ≥ 1, and δ = 2^(−b), the explicit-arithmetic, ideal exact-angle algorithm uses O(n²b) controlled modular-multiplier circuits, O(n⁴b) elementary gates, and O(n⁴b) schoolbook classical bit transitions. With only controlled-U_x access, its query count is exactly t(Q − 1), where t = 4(n + 1)b and Q = 2^(2n + 3). No finite-alphabet, uniform-family, or generator-time bound is asserted.

seams_checked.note: Checked the QPE procedure, circular-distance definition, superposition law, nearest-grid guarantee, and access-cost theorem. The orbit Fourier sign yields positive eigenphase k/r; the consumer uses an eigenspace mixture and preserves the distinction between powered access and repeated base-unitary queries.

The explicit bounded-fanin Boolean DAG meets the reversible compiler interface, including repeated-source ports. Both XOR computations restore their work, and compute-swap-inverse clears the target. Compiler gate/work bounds are used with the stated output width.
Dirac notation is compatible with the root inner product being linear in its first argument. The orbit eigenvector and orthogonality calculations preserve that convention.
The multiplier's chronological compute, swap, and cleanup sequence agrees with the circuit-denotation convention. QPE measurement is consumed through its stated outcome law.

Register port order remains big-endian despite least-significant-first internal arithmetic arrays. Valid and invalid encodings partition the full data basis, and the orbit calculation uses distinct orthonormal computational-basis vectors.

The cost consumer keeps elementary gates, clean workspace, oracle queries, description generation, and classical work separate. It explicitly limits its QFT count to ideal exact-angle gates and makes no uniform-family claim.
Classical arithmetic is charged in the declared multitape transition model. Reconstruction, inverse preprocessing, and modular verification are counted separately from quantum gates and oracle calls.

The factoring algorithm establishes unit membership before calling order finding with b = 2. Its success proof uses the pointwise exact-order probability of at least 3/4; its cost theorem preserves the ideal-QFT qualification and exponential bare-unitary query count.
The discrete-logarithm success theorem applies φ(q)/q ≥ 1/(1 + log₂q) with integer q ≥ 2. It does not import an order-finding oracle or stronger arithmetic interface from this batch.
